note: THE ONLY THING A MODEL EVER SEES ABOUT THE CLASSIFICATION FOOTNOTE. One row per KIND of uncorroborated label the site can draw, never one row per spacecraft: there are eight kinds and 1,559 marked cards, and a footnote written per card would be 1,559 chances to say something the facts do not support. Every sentence below is a restatement of what pipeline/build_release.py actually recorded for that basis, and of CLASSIFICATION_BASIS_EVIDENCE in src/main.ts, which is the sentence already printed on the card as 'Category evidence'. `what` and `notChecked` are the MATERIAL. `mustBelieve` and `mustNotBelieve` are TESTS on the finished footnote, not sentences to print - the first live run (2026-08-27) printed all four as four sentences in order, blew every word budget, and read like a form, which is why the last two are named the way they are now.
deterministicFallbackIsAbsentOnPurpose: The sentence that ships when the model is down is NOT in this file. Shown its own fallback, a model hands it straight back: the result passes every gate, because it is made of these facts, and ships marked as model-written while the model authored nothing. narration/build_hedge_footnotes.py composes the fallback from `what` + `notChecked`, and refuses to mark a line as model-written if it comes back as that composition.
takenFrom: src/main.ts CLASSIFICATION_BASIS_EVIDENCE / CORROBORATED_BASES / classificationChipEvidence, and the live catalog at public/data/artifacts/catalog-574094c018fc8cd5.json
audience: A reader who has just noticed an asterisk on a label and wants to know what it means. Not a specialist.

keys.what: The label comes from this spacecraft's name matching the naming pattern of a known programme.
keys.notChecked: Nothing about this individual spacecraft was checked against an operator, a government or an independent observer.
keys.mustBelieve: Spacecraft named into this programme do this job.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That anyone outside this site has confirmed the job for this particular spacecraft.

keys.what: Named independent analysts worked out what this spacecraft is for, from its orbit and its launch.
keys.notChecked: No operator and no government has published what this spacecraft is for.
keys.mustBelieve: The site is repeating a published assessment made by analysts who never had official confirmation either.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That the country flying the spacecraft has said what it does.

keys.what: Named independent analysts worked out what this spacecraft is for, from its orbit and its launch.
keys.notChecked: No operator and no government has published what this spacecraft is for, and the reviewer who recorded the analysts' reading here marked the answer as still unsettled.
keys.mustBelieve: The site is repeating the best published reading of a spacecraft nobody has explained.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That the reading is settled, or that the country flying the spacecraft has said what it does.

keys.what: The label comes from the category the orbit catalogue files this object under.
keys.notChecked: Nothing was checked against the spacecraft itself.
keys.mustBelieve: One catalogue sorts this object into this category.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That anybody examined this spacecraft and agreed with that sorting.

keys.what: This spacecraft's name matched a known programme.
keys.notChecked: Two independent sources say that name belongs to a different spacecraft, so the match was withdrawn and nothing replaced it.
keys.mustBelieve: The label is the one the catalogue offers, and the site does not stand behind it.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That this object is the spacecraft the name points at.

keys.what: No source this site consulted establishes what this spacecraft is for.
keys.notChecked: No operator filing, no independent observation and no analyst's reading was found for it.
keys.mustBelieve: The label above is a placeholder for an object the site could not identify.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That this is what the spacecraft does.

keys.what: A rule written for this specific object put the label on it.
keys.notChecked: The reviewer who wrote that rule recorded that the answer is still not settled, which is why the mark stays.
keys.mustBelieve: The label is this site's own reading of the object, written down as unsure.

keys.what: This release does not record how the label was arrived at.
keys.notChecked: Nothing is recorded as having been checked against this spacecraft.
keys.mustBelieve: The label is carried forward from the catalogue as it was found.
keys.mustNotBelieve: That anything about it has been checked.

budgetNote: TWO NUMBERS, BECAUSE ONE NUMBER WAS A LIE. The first live runs were given a single `wordBudget` of 40 and landed at 42-56 words, writing exactly the two-sentence footnote that was asked for. Enforcing 40 would have thrown away eight good footnotes over a number nobody had checked against real output; quietly enforcing 60 while the prompt said 40 is the gate-disagrees-with-the-prompt trap that the layer-narration lane paid for on its first day. So `wordAim` is the length to write to and `wordCeiling` is the number narration/build_hedge_footnotes.py actually enforces, and the prompt says both.
